# Class 9 physics, ~1.5 minutes, written by Claude for F-014 S0 (Concept Simulation). Spoken values as Whisper writes
# them. Expect: a block-on-a-surface simulation (5 kg, mu 0.2, push 20 N: moves, a = 2.04 m/s^2), the switch to an
# incline (30 degrees, mass and mu carried: slides, a = 3.21 m/s^2), then a 20 N push up the slope (at rest). The
# "friction force ... 9.8 newtons" line is a result, not a push: it must not change F.
@setup subject=Physics grade=9 topic="Friction and the inclined plane"

Good morning class. Today we will study friction and the inclined plane.
[pause 1]
Friction is the force that opposes relative motion between two surfaces in contact.
It always acts along the surface, against the motion or against the tendency to move.
[pause 1.5]
Consider a block of mass 5 kg resting on a rough floor.
The coefficient of friction between the block and the floor is 0.2.
Now we push it with a force of 20 newtons.
The friction force is mu times the normal force, which is about 9.8 newtons, so the block speeds up.
[pause 2]
Now let us tilt the surface.
Imagine the same block on an inclined plane at 30 degrees.
The weight now has a component m g sine theta along the slope, and m g cos theta into the surface.
With a coefficient of friction of 0.2 the block slides down the slope.
[pause 1.5]
What if we push it up the slope with 20 newtons? Let's see what happens.
The push and the friction together balance the pull down the slope, so the block stays at rest.
[pause 1]
That is how the inclined plane works. Next class we will look at pulleys.
